items.question: How can Indian manufacturers find international buyers between trade shows?
items.answer: Map the companies in one export market that buy your product category, then contact their procurement and technical heads with your certifications and capacity up front. An Indian precision components maker targeting German machinery companies booked 18 meetings, 6 requests for quotation and 3 sample requests this way, outside the exhibition calendar.

items.question: Do you work with our specific product category?
items.answer: Very likely. We have run campaigns across auto components, textiles, industrial equipment, packaging, engineering goods and food processing. During onboarding we map your product to the right buyer profile in your target markets, so the outreach speaks to how that category is sourced, not to manufacturing in general.

items.question: How do you make sure buyers are serious and not just price shopping?
items.answer: We target named procurement heads, sourcing managers and importers directly, chosen by company size and buying signals, instead of broadcasting to anyone who fills a form on a B2B portal. Outreach asks about real requirements, such as volumes and certifications, so price-only enquiries are easy to spot early.

items.question: Which countries and regions can you target?
items.answer: We have run outreach across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia, including Germany, France and the UAE. Tell us your target markets and we build the prospect list and messaging around them, with sends timed to each region's working hours and copy that reads naturally to buyers there.

items.question: Do you handle the language and cultural side of outreach in different markets?
items.answer: Yes. Messaging tone and structure are adjusted per region, and we can localise outreach where needed so it reads naturally to buyers in that market. That covers details such as formality, how the first email opens and which proof points a buyer in that region expects to see.

items.question: What does pricing and commitment look like?
items.answer: We work on a monthly retainer with a 3-month minimum, which covers setup and enough sending to judge results. After that it runs month to month with 30 days' notice, with no annual contract. We don't publish a price list; we share a quote after a free GTM audit call, once we know which channels you need.

items.question: What happens once we get an interested buyer? Do you help close the deal?
items.answer: Closing stays with your team. We hand over every qualified meeting with full context on the buyer and their requirements, such as volumes, specifications and timelines, so your team can focus on samples, pricing and the relationship. We keep following up with the prospects who have not replied yet.
